children: India's FMCG stocks, Dabur Ltd., Hindustan Unilever Ltd. (HUL), ITC Ltd., Britannia Ltd., have all gained between 3% to 7% through the course of the week, and are trading with modest losses on Friday, November 27, after the recent Supreme Court ruling.
Shares of Britannia, Dabur, Marico, GCPL are trading with losses between 0.5% to 1%, while those of ITC are trading just above the flat line.

In a significant move impacting the packaged food and beverage industry, the Supreme Court has mandated stricter front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FOPL) rules. Food and beverage products exceeding prescribed nutritional thresholds will now be required to carry distinct, front-facing warning labels, ensuring greater transparency for consumers.

According to the Supreme Court directive, packaged products exceeding prescribed limits must display separate hexagonal warning labels for each specific nutrient of concern, such as High Fat, High Sodium, and High Sugar.
The threshold assessments must be based on total sugar, fat, and salt content in the product, rather than solely accounting for added amounts.
The Supreme Court rejected proposals for a phased implementation, directing a uniform, single-stage rollout across the industry.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has been directed to release a revised draft notification within 10 weeks and complete the finalization of the norms within 4 months. Once the standards are rolled out, food companies will be granted a 365-day transition window to comply with the updated packaging requirements.

The Nifty FMCG index has risen 2.5% so far this year. Shares of Dabur and Britannia have gained 6.5% and 6% respectively for the week so far, while those of HUL, GCPL and ITC are up between 3% to 3.5%.

title: FMCG Stocks Dabur, HUL, ITC, Britannia have had a good week - Here's why they are in the news
